title: Adaptive sampler orchestration + CI collector harness
content:
Purpose:
This doc describes an end-to-end CI-first harness for orchestrating sampled runtime captures across variants of the serving runtime. The goal is to produce consistently-shaped artifacts (perf.data, pprof, lightweight traces, flamegraph SVGs, and KV-cache snapshots) from short reproducible runs so we can:

- Detect regressions in tail-latency and allocation hotspots in CI.
- Correlate request shapes with backend behavior (e.g., KV cache misses, kv cache eviction spikes).
- Produce human-readable artifacts for postmortem and perf-oncall.

Design overview (high level):
1) Coordinator: a small Python service that receives a CI trigger (PR or nightly) and decides which sampler job to run. It uses a repo-level config (ci-sampler.yaml) describing workloads and target nodes.
2) Lightweight agent (container): runs inside the target test pod. Responsible for: starting the synthetic workload, capturing perf/profiler artifacts, snapshotting in-memory caches, and uploading artifacts to GCS/S3.
3) Aggregator: pulls artifacts, runs post-processing (flamegraph generation, symbolization, off-cpu aggregation), and publishes summary reports.

Principles and constraints:
- Runs should be cheap (<= 3 minutes per target) so they can live in PR checks.
- Determinism where possible: fixed RNG seeds for synthetic workloads, stabilized model weights (small distilled checkpoints) to keep runtime code paths consistent.
- Keep traces small: sample-based captures with adaptive duration (see sampling policy below).
- Clear artifact naming conventions so triage is fast.

Sampling policy (adaptive):
- Warmup phase (30s): run low-concurrency workload to populate caches. No perf capture.
- Sampling phase (60s): run workload at target QPS and do sample-based captures. Dynamically increase sample frequency if observed latency > latency-SLO threshold.
- Cooldown/flush (15s): capture KV-cache snapshot and metadata.

Config example (ci-sampler.yaml snippet):
workloads:
  - id: http-short-llm
    qps: 75
    concurrency: 8
    sequence_lengths: [64, 128]
    seed: 4091
    collector_profile: perf-sampled
  - id: cold-start-reqs
    qps: 2
    concurrency: 1
    collector_profile: startup-trace

collector_profile definitions:
- perf-sampled: uses `perf record -F 99 -g -p <pid>` inside the container with --call-graph dwarf when supported. Falls back to perf + addr2line symbolization in CI.
- offcpu-ebpf: uses the eBPF off-cpu toolchain (kubectl + privileged helper image) for threads blocked on io/locks.
- startup-trace: full single-run capture (strace + light flamegraph) for cold-start debugging.

Artifact naming (important):
<pr|nightly>_<workload>_<nodepool>_<commit-sha>_<timestamp>_<collector>.tar.gz
Example: PR-1027_http-short-llm_g2-2x_9af3b2c_20241008T1302_perf.tar.gz
Inside the tarball we expect:
- perf.data (raw record)
- pprof.pb or pprof.txt (converted)
- flamegraph.svg
- kvcache-snapshot.jsonl (if requested)
- metadata.json (env, args, git ref, workload seed, QPS, concurrency, node labels)

CI integration (Github Actions):
- jobs: sampler-coordinator (runs on matrix of targets). Each job spins up test cluster nodepool via infra CI step, applies test manifests, and launches the sampler agent as a sidecar or initContainer depending on profile.
- artifact upload: use actions/upload-artifact for short-term, plus a background uploader to GCS for retention.
- gating: required for perf-critical PRs (tagged with `perf-check`) or nightly for full matrix.

Collector implementation notes and run commands:
- perf (container-based):
  * Ensure container image includes linux-tools and addr2line.
  * Command (inside container):
    perf record -F 99 -g -p $PID -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep $DURATION
    perf script -i /tmp/perf.data | /usr/local/bin/stackcollapse-perf.pl > /tmp/perf.folded
    /usr/local/bin/flamegraph.pl /tmp/perf.folded > /tmp/flamegraph.svg
- eBPF offcpu: run from privileged helper pod in same node. Use BCC or libbpf-based off-cpu collector. Collect until the sampling phase ends, then pull /tmp/offcpu.pb.
- minimal symbolization: ship binaries with e.g. .debug_info stripped out? For CI we keep a lightweight debug bundle per build in the artifacts store to map addresses.

Post-processing pipeline (aggregator):
- Validate artifact structure and metadata.
- Run symbolizer to produce annotated pprof. For non-dwarf builds fallback to address->line mapping using build-id cache.
- Generate diffable summaries: top-10 functions by CPU, by self-time, by allocs, and off-cpu top waiters.
- Produce a single HTML report with embedded flamegraph and a short automated blurb comparing baseline commit (branch base) to PR commit.

Interpretation heuristics (quick triage):
- sudden shift of 20%+ of CPU to different call chain -> suspicious code or kernel change
- increase in syscalls per token (read/write/open/unlink) -> IO amplification regressions or logging spam
- repeated stacks that show time in GC/allocator -> memory pressure OR increased allocations in hot loop
- cache-miss spikes in metadata.json with kvcache hit-rate drop correlate with higher p99 latency

Runbook: How to run locally (dev loop)
1) Build local dev image: `make image-dev`
2) Start a minikube (or k3d) cluster with node labels matching `nodepool:ci-small`
3) `kubectl apply -f deploy/ci-sampler-agent.yaml`
4) Trigger coordinator: `python tools/ci-sampler/coordinator.py --workload http-short-llm --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD)`
5) After completion, `./tools/ci-sampler/collector-fetcher.py --artifact <name>` to pull artifacts and `./tools/ci-sampler/aggregate.py --input <tarball>` to produce HTML.

Known trouble and debugging tips:
- Symptom: perf.data exists but flamegraph is blank
Fix: check that addr2line is present and build-id bundle was uploaded for that commit. If no debug symbols, run `perf script -i perf.data | c++filt` to at least get demangled names.
- Symptom: noisy kernel stacks dominating time
Fix: use `--no-children` and try `-F 199` to reduce aggregation bias, or enable eBPF off-cpu to separate user vs kernel.
- Symptom: inconsistent artifact sizes across runs
Fix: validate that the coordinator applied the same RNG seed and the same model checkpoint. Check metadata.json.

Progress checklist (open items):
- [ ] Add automatic baseline selection: choose last green main build for diffs. (ENG-1872)
- [ ] Harden uploader to retry on transient GCS failures. (Marco)
- [ ] Add a lightweight JS flamegraph viewer to the HTML report for quicker zooming. (Priya)
- [ ] Integrate with Slack perf-alerts for PRs that regress p95/p99. (Ethan)

Notes to self and follow-ups:
- We should avoid long-running privileged pods in PR CI; prefer transient helper nodes created by infra.
- Consider store minimal obfuscated debug bundles instead of keeping full .debug in CI images — reduces image size and still enables symbolization.
- Add a mode that only runs on Dedicated pools to compare different GPU kernels.

References and commands (clipboard):
- local flamegraph tools: https://github.com/brendangregg/FlameGraph
- perf->flame instructions: https://perf.wiki.kernel.org/index.php/Tutorial
- off-cpu tooling: https://github.com/iovisor/bpftrace (helper scripts in repo)

Appendix: minimal collector container Dockerfile (dev):
FROM ubuntu:22.04
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y linux-tools-common linux-tools-generic linux-tools-$(uname -r) binutils addr2line python3 
COPY tools/ci-sampler/* /usr/local/bin/
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/ci-sampler-agent"]

End of doc.
